idiom_name: callable factories - pass the creator (e.g. json.loads(parse_float=Decimal))
implementation_notes: Python's first-class functions and classes make the factory hierarchy unnecessary in the common case: hand the creators to the code that needs them (json.loads(parse_float=Decimal), object_hook, a class or a small dict of functions) and the family is whatever bundle you passed. python-patterns.guide rates the full pattern as a poor fit for Python, an awkward workaround for missing first-class functions; use abc.ABC with @abstractmethod only when the contract must be enforced for third-party families or isinstance dispatch is required.
pitfalls: Mutable class attributes used as creators are shared by every caller; keep them immutable/staticmethod functions.

A lambda is generally not picklable by reference, while functools.partial is picklable when its wrapped callable and bound arguments are picklable; use module-level creators and serializable arguments for worker boundaries.
Nothing enforces the product contract in the callable style - a creator with the wrong arity fails deep inside client code; document the signature or add a Protocol.
Mutable class attributes used as creators are shared by every caller; keep them immutable or expose per-instance/static creator functions.
Nothing enforces the product contract in the callable style: a creator with the wrong arity or return type fails deep inside client code; document signatures or add a Protocol.
The callable style cannot enforce abstract methods at runtime; use abc.ABC plus @abstractmethod when third-party plugins need instantiation checks, otherwise keep the lighter callable contract.

variants.name: abc.ABC hierarchy with abstract factory methods
variants.implementation_notes: When the family contract must be enforced (plugin authors, multiple implementation modules, isinstance-based dispatch), declare an ABC with one @abstractmethod per product kind: the metaclass refuses to instantiate an incomplete family with a TypeError, which the duck-typed variant cannot do. Concrete families subclass it and only they import the concrete products. Use this form when the extra ceremony buys real safety; for two callables it is pure overhead.
pitfalls: abstractmethod only affects regular subclassing: classes registered via ABC.register() bypass the check, so register() defeats the enforcement.
Abstract methods may still carry a super()-callable implementation, which subclasses can silently rely on instead of overriding - document that the body is a hook.
Metaclass conflicts appear when an ABC is mixed with a class using a different metaclass; prefer abc.ABC over bare ABCMeta.
